# DevOps by hmrdkn-labs

> Question-first, portable DevOps learning material. Prose is CC BY-SA 4.0; code is MIT.

- [Cloud-native architecture principles](https://devops.hamardikan.com/raw/v1/units/cloud-native-architecture-principles/unit.md): Understand cloud-native systems as loosely coupled, declarative, observable, resilient, automated systems rather than as applications that merely happen to run in a cloud.
- [CI, CD, declarative delivery, and GitOps](https://devops.hamardikan.com/raw/v1/units/cloud-native-delivery-gitops/unit.md): Distinguish artifact creation from release reconciliation and explain how GitOps turns version-controlled desired state into continuously reconciled application delivery.
- [Metrics, logs, traces, events, and observability](https://devops.hamardikan.com/raw/v1/units/cloud-native-observability-signals/unit.md): Use metrics, logs, traces, Kubernetes events, and end-to-end probes as complementary evidence rather than treating one monitoring tool as complete observability.
- [Release strategies and application debugging](https://devops.hamardikan.com/raw/v1/units/cloud-native-release-debugging/unit.md): Distinguish rolling, blue-green, and canary release ideas and debug a failed Kubernetes release from artifact through rollout, readiness, endpoints, and user traffic.
- [CNCF ecosystem, projects, standards, and community](https://devops.hamardikan.com/raw/v1/units/cncf-ecosystem-community/unit.md): Place Kubernetes within the CNCF ecosystem, recognize common project responsibilities, and distinguish open interfaces, project maturity, community governance, and the landscape catalog.
- [Configuration, secrets, and persistent storage](https://devops.hamardikan.com/raw/v1/units/config-secrets-storage/unit.md): Separate non-secret configuration, sensitive values, and stateful volume lifecycle while respecting identity and topology.
- [Container runtime and lifecycle](https://devops.hamardikan.com/raw/v1/units/container-lifecycle/unit.md): Connect an image to the runtime-created process, writable layer, isolation settings, logs, exit status, and restart behavior.
- [Container networking and storage](https://devops.hamardikan.com/raw/v1/units/container-network-storage/unit.md): Follow interfaces, published ports, bind mounts, and volumes across the isolation boundary of a container.
- [Files, users, and permissions](https://devops.hamardikan.com/raw/v1/units/files-users-permissions/unit.md): Understand Linux paths, ownership, mode bits, and why service identity is part of both reliability and security.
- [Git, YAML, and declarative intent](https://devops.hamardikan.com/raw/v1/units/git-yaml-declarative/unit.md): Use versioned text to express desired state while respecting YAML types, schema validation, review, and reconciliation.
- [HTTP requests and TLS identity](https://devops.hamardikan.com/raw/v1/units/http-tls/unit.md): Trace application requests above TCP and understand the separate guarantees provided by TLS encryption and certificate identity.
- [Container images, layers, and registries](https://devops.hamardikan.com/raw/v1/units/images-layers-registries/unit.md): Treat an image as immutable content plus configuration, then reason about layers, tags, digests, and supply-chain movement.
- [IP addresses and subnets](https://devops.hamardikan.com/raw/v1/units/ip-subnets/unit.md): Reason about interface addresses, prefixes, local delivery, and the route choice behind every packet.
- [KCNA domain map and reasoning strategy](https://devops.hamardikan.com/raw/v1/units/kcna-domain-map/unit.md): Map the current KCNA blueprint to a small set of Kubernetes and cloud-native mental models so study is driven by reasoning rather than isolated terms.
- [KCNA Kubernetes Fundamentals quiz companion](https://devops.hamardikan.com/raw/v1/units/kcna-kubernetes-fundamentals-review/unit.md): A fast review of containers, orchestration, Kubernetes architecture, CRI, and container runtimes for use beside the KCNA fundamentals quiz.
- [KCNA Kubernetes Resources quiz companion](https://devops.hamardikan.com/raw/v1/units/kcna-kubernetes-resources-review/unit.md): A compact review of Pods, YAML objects, ReplicaSets, Deployments, rollouts, apply, imperative versus declarative management, kubectl explain, and namespaces.
- [kubectl apply and live state](https://devops.hamardikan.com/raw/v1/units/kubernetes-apply-live-state/unit.md): Treat kubectl apply as declarative API reconciliation, compare local intent with live state, and understand why successful configuration is only one proof layer.
- [Kubernetes components and the API request path](https://devops.hamardikan.com/raw/v1/units/kubernetes-architecture-components/unit.md): Trace a Kubernetes change from kubectl through the API, control-plane reconciliation, scheduling, kubelet execution, runtime, and status feedback.
- [Kubernetes API and control loops](https://devops.hamardikan.com/raw/v1/units/kubernetes-control-loop/unit.md): Understand Kubernetes as an API-driven system where controllers continuously reconcile declared intent with observed state.
- [Deployments, rollouts, and rollbacks](https://devops.hamardikan.com/raw/v1/units/kubernetes-deployments-rollouts/unit.md): Trace how a Deployment manages ReplicaSets, why template changes create rollout revisions, and how rollout evidence differs from application health.
- [Labels, selectors, and ReplicaSets](https://devops.hamardikan.com/raw/v1/units/kubernetes-labels-replicasets/unit.md): Connect label-based selection to ReplicaSet ownership and explain how a controller continuously repairs replica-count drift.
- [Kubernetes manifests and API objects](https://devops.hamardikan.com/raw/v1/units/kubernetes-manifests/unit.md): Read a Kubernetes manifest as a request to the API, separate desired spec from observed status, and prove what the cluster accepted.
- [Kubernetes namespaces and API scope](https://devops.hamardikan.com/raw/v1/units/kubernetes-namespaces-scope/unit.md): Use namespaces as namespaced API scope and organizational boundaries while avoiding the common mistake of treating a namespace as automatic security isolation.
- [Kubernetes networking request path](https://devops.hamardikan.com/raw/v1/units/kubernetes-networking-request-path/unit.md): Trace a request from DNS through a Service and EndpointSlice to a Pod while separating CNI connectivity, Service forwarding, ingress routing, and policy.
- [Pod model, lifecycle, and ownership](https://devops.hamardikan.com/raw/v1/units/kubernetes-pod-model/unit.md): Reason about Pods as disposable execution records with one scheduled node, shared network identity, lifecycle phases, and controller ownership.
- [Kubernetes scheduling and placement constraints](https://devops.hamardikan.com/raw/v1/units/kubernetes-scheduling-placement/unit.md): Predict where a Pod can run by separating resource requests, node selection, affinity, taints and tolerations, topology spreading, and controller intent.
- [Kubernetes identity, authorization, admission, and workload boundaries](https://devops.hamardikan.com/raw/v1/units/kubernetes-security-access/unit.md): Separate authentication, RBAC authorization, admission, workload identity, Secret handling, Pod security, and network segmentation into clear security boundaries.
- [Kubernetes persistent storage lifecycle](https://devops.hamardikan.com/raw/v1/units/kubernetes-storage-lifecycle/unit.md): Trace durable storage from a workload claim through StorageClass and CSI provisioning to a bound volume, mounted Pod, topology constraints, and reclaim behavior.
- [Namespaces and control groups](https://devops.hamardikan.com/raw/v1/units/namespaces-cgroups/unit.md): See containers as ordinary processes given scoped views and enforceable resource boundaries by the Linux kernel.
- [Pods and workload controllers](https://devops.hamardikan.com/raw/v1/units/pods-workloads/unit.md): Choose the smallest Kubernetes execution unit and the controller whose identity and replacement semantics match the workload.
- [Ports, sockets, and DNS](https://devops.hamardikan.com/raw/v1/units/ports-sockets-dns/unit.md): Connect process sockets to transport ports and use DNS as name-to-record lookup rather than magical connectivity.
- [Processes and finite resources](https://devops.hamardikan.com/raw/v1/units/processes-and-resources/unit.md): Build the mental model that every service is a process competing for CPU time, memory, files, and input/output.
- [Routing, NAT, and firewalls](https://devops.hamardikan.com/raw/v1/units/routing-nat-firewalls/unit.md): Follow packet decisions through routes, address translation, and stateful policy without collapsing them into one network box.
- [Scheduling, resources, and health probes](https://devops.hamardikan.com/raw/v1/units/scheduling-resources-health/unit.md): Relate placement to requests, runtime enforcement to limits, and traffic or restart decisions to distinct health signals.
- [Services, cluster DNS, and ingress](https://devops.hamardikan.com/raw/v1/units/services-dns-ingress/unit.md): Separate changing Pod endpoints from stable service discovery and north-south HTTP routing through implementing controllers.
- [Shells, pipes, exit status, and signals](https://devops.hamardikan.com/raw/v1/units/shell-pipes-signals/unit.md): Treat the shell as a process launcher and composition tool, then reason precisely about streams, status, and shutdown.
- [Troubleshoot from process to pod](https://devops.hamardikan.com/raw/v1/units/troubleshoot-process-to-pod/unit.md): Localize failures with an evidence ladder that moves from desired state to process, network, policy, and user-visible behavior.
